findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: No certified food protection manager (CFPM) was observed in the facility at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED: The CFPM showed up later during the inspection. The inspector discussed with the person-in-charge (PIC) to have another employee certified in food protection management, so that a CFPM can be present during hours of operation. Ensure a CFPM is available at the facility during all hours of food preparation.
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: A stack of plastic containers were observed on the edge of the designated handwashing sink by the three-compartment sink. CORRECTED: The PIC removed the containers after being informed by the inspector. Ensure the handwashing sink is easily accessible at all times.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [PF]

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: No ambient thermometers were observed in the walk-in and bottom of the pizza prep table coolers. The PIC was informed and instructed to provide internal thermometers in each cooler to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the warmest part of each cooler to accurately monitor internal temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The wall tiles under the soap dispenser, between the handwashing sink and pizza prep table was observed to be breaking from the wall at the top and the surface. The PIC was informed to have the tiles caulked back to the wall. Ensure the wall tiles are replaced for easy cleaning and also to prevent possible hideout for pests.
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: A wet mop head was observed stored on the surface of the mop sink with the mop head facing downward.  CORRECTED - The PIC was informed that mop heads must be stored in a manner that allows for proper air-drying. The mop head was placed on the wringer basket by the PIC to facilitate adequate air-drying. Ensure mop heads are properly stored by placing them in the wringer basket or hanging them to air-dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
An employee handling food was observed to have an expired food handlers’ certificate (expired 3 years ago). The PIC stated the employee has been scheduled to take the certified food protection manager class on March 4, 2026.  The inspector instructed the PIC to ensure all employees handling foods are certified in safe food handling. Ensure all food handlers obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed manager at beginning of inspection to indicate he had cold-like symptoms similar to COVID-19. Inspector asked if the employee had been instructed to stay home and get tested for COVID-19. Employee indicated the management had not instructed him to do so. Inspector contacted SCDPH and infectious disease nurses instructed Inspector to tell employee to leave immediately and get tested for COVID-19. Employee should not return to work until a negative COVID-19 test is confirmed and/or quarantine procedures are followed. Inspector will follow-up with the district manager about this employee on 6/30/21.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Observed NO paper towels throughout the facility at all hand sinks. Upon asking employees about the lack of paper towels, employee stated that they ran out and the order was coming in two days. Inspector instructed employees to put napkins at all hand sinks in the mean time. Employee was sent to buy paper towels for the facility. Discussed proper stocking of hand sinks with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed the walk-in cooler to be not functioning appropriately. Walk-in cooler was holding temperature at 48-52 degrees F. MB Heating and Cooling was called for an emergency service on the walk-in cooler. MB Heating and Cooling was actively working to correct the cooler during the voluntary destruction of foods. All TCS foods with temperatures 45 degrees F or above were discarded voluntarily due to walk-in cooler holding above 45 degrees F for longer than 24 hours. It has been 3 days since the cooler had began to fail, 6/25/21. This was indicated by the digital temperature checking system. See attached photo page. 

Areas of the walk-in cooler had different temperatures. Towards the back of the walk-in cooler, items were colder and thawing from freezing temperatures. Temperatures near the front of the cooler were warmer due to the nature of the cooler door being next to these foods. Bags of shreded provolone and mozzarella were found to be thawing and within temperature. 

Items near the back of the walk-in cooler that were out of temperature: ham, beef patty crumbles, boneless chicken wings, shaved beef slices, pepperoni, chicken wings, hard salami - between 45 degrees to 48 degrees F.

Items near the front of the walk-in cooler on the right that were out of temperature: portioned foods (ham, beef sausage crumbles, grilled chicken, philly steak, pepperoni, Italian sausage, pasta sauce, diced tomatoes - between 47 degrees to 53 degrees F. Other items on this shelf included: feta, blue cheese dip, spinach, pre-cooked pasta - between 47 degrees and 51 degrees F.

Items near the front of the walk-in cooler on the left side that were out of temperature: chicken Caesar salad, garden salad, Alfredo sauce, garlic Parmesan sauce, sliced provolone cheese, ranch, pizza sauce, and sliced American cheese - between 45 degrees and 52 degrees F. 

All items were probed manually throughout the voluntary destruction of food. 

Certain foods were not TCS and remained in walk-in cooler: fully cooked bacon, cut green peppers, cut onion, pineapple, banana peppers, jalapeños, anchovies, parmasan cheese (grated, dry), dough, cake, brownies, fresh mushrooms, mango habanera sauce, ketchup mustard sauce, hot sauce. 

Inspector will follow-up regarding temperature of walk-in cooler on 6/30/21. Until walk-in cooler is functioning appropriately, cease use of the cooler for TCS foods. Items that were in good temperature were taken to the bottom prep coolers to store. Store currently is not operating for customers. Next shipment is due on Wednesday, per employee, 6/30/21.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy, nor a method to clean for vomit and diarrhea. Provided copy of policy and discussed with PIC. Discussed that a bodily fluid clean-up kit may be purchased instead of utilizing bleach and the policy provided. Facility currently does not have bleach to perform procedure. Inspector will follow-up on 4/22/21.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-202.12: (A) HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water of a temperature at least 100F through mixing valve. Pf (B) Steam mixing valve may not be used. (C) A self-closing, slow-closing, or metered faucet shall provide at least 15 seconds of flowing water. (D) An automatic sink shall be installed to manufacturer’s guidelines. 

Observed hand washing sink in back kitchen to have no hot water. Inspector tried both faucet handles - one barely turns on and the other only produces cold water after ~3-5 minutes running. Both customer bathrooms do not have hot water as well. Water was left on for roughly ~3-5 minutes. Hand sink in front prep area does have hot water. Utilized this hand sink only until repairs are conducted to the back hand sink. Employee's should wash their hands with the front prep hand sink after returning from the bathrooms. Inspector will follow-up on 4/22/21.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

Observed three containers of beef within walk-in cooler to have an expiration date of 4/10/21 - two days past the seven day date marking rule. Discussed with PIC. Ensure foods that are expired are thrown away by expiration date. COS.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
3-302.12: If in working container, FOOD not readily recognized or easily mistakable shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. 

(REPEAT) Observed corn meal for pizza prep to be contained in large storage container without common name of item. Discussed need for common name label on product. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/28/2020.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-303.12: (A) PACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if FOOD is subject to entry of water. (B) unPACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in contact with undrained ice. (C) Whole raw produce, cut, raw vegetables such as celery, carrots, potatoes, or tofu can be immersed in ice or water. (D) Raw poultry and raw FISH received in ice may remain in condition while in storage awaiting preparation, display, service, or sale. 

Observed pooling water at the base of the bottom prep cooler nearest the front hand sink. Water is pooling then freezing over. Food prep items are being stored in this prep cooler - containers of shred cheese at time of inspection. Ensure repairs are conducted and food is not in contact with ponding water/ice.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

(REPEAT) Observed handle of the corn meal scoop to be within the corn meal inside the storage container. Discussed with PIC that the handle should be above the top of the food item. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/28/2020.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair. 

Observed bottom of the prep cooler to have ponding water that is frozen over on the base of the cooler - prep cooler closest to the front hand sink. Frozen water is in contact with food items - shred cheese in container. Discussed need for repairs with PIC. Repair according to Illinois and local plumbing codes.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

Observed caulk at 3 compartment sink to no longer be smooth and easily cleanable. Caulk is coming away from the wall and sink. Re-caulk and repair as needed.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Observed mop to be stored within the mop bucket in a manner that does not allow to air dry. Discussed mop drying with PIC - must be hung in a manner that allows to drip or air dry. COS.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

(REPEAT) Observed facility to have no food handler's licenses available to view during inspection. Discussed creating a PH folder with food handler's (and CFPM's) licenses. Secondary employee who was not PIC - unsure if has food handler's license. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/28/2020.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)

750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

PIC on duty stated she was a CFM and facility district manager has her enrolled in a new CFM training class for February. PIC was unable to produce certificate during inspection. Ensure all manager's on duty have CFM training and licensure, as well as having copies readily available to view.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:

Observed no quaternary ammonium sanitizer within 3 compartment sink at back dish location. Facility found sanitizer and filled that compartment of sink to appropriate levels, 300 ppm. findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food utensil storage bins are not clean to sight and touch. Wash, rinse, sanitize routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

Observed multiple food utensil storage bins to have food debris and/or splash within the bins. Discussed routine cleaning of storage bin trays with PIC.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204-112  (C) A thermometer is not provided in the prep cooler. Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Reference 4-204-112.

Observed one of the prep coolers to be missing a thermometer in the bottom level. Discussed purchasing thermometer for the bottom prep cooler with PIC.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

Observed several in-use wiping rags to be stored outside sanitizer solution. Facility does not use sanitizer buckets; rather, sanitizer spray. Discussed with PIC that single-use paper towels should be used with spray. COS.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12  (C) In-Use Utensils are stored incorrectly in the corn meal storage container. Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

Observed the handle of the corn meal scoop to be within the corn meal in the storage container. Discussed with PIC that the handle should be above the top of the food item. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on bottom prep cooler shelves. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11  (C) Caulk of front hand sink was found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed caulk of front hand sink to be coming away from the wall and sink. Discussed repairs with PIC.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

Observed build-up of food splash on wall near front hand sink, as well as sneeze guards of prep area. Discussed routine cleaning of physical facilities with PIC.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-501.110  (C) Employees were found not using the designated dressing rooms / changing areas or designated employees lockers when changing clothes or storing personal articles. Dressing rooms and lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used if employees regularly change clothes or store personal articles in the establishment while working. Reference 6-501.110.

Observed personal coat to be hanging on and near empty pizza boxes in the back area. Discussed with employee that coats should be in a designated area and/or office area. COS.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  Reference 410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430.

Observed employee to state he had food handlers licensure; however, facility and employee were unable to procure proof of license. Discussed with employee to keep a copy on hand, as well as maintain license every 3 years.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Observed unlidded employee beverage stored on pizza cutting prep table upon entering establishment. Noted utensil storage and active food preparation on same table. Drink was discarded by staff. 
->Provide designated area for drinking. Store in a manner to prevent contamination from food, food preparation areas, and clean utensils.   Reference 2-401.11.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Large container of marinara sauce measured at 55F stored on preparation table in back area. PIC indicated sauce is luke warm water mixed with Dominos prepackaged sauce mix, which is then left out for 2 hours until it is moved into cold holding.  Discussed proper cold holding temperatures/procedures with PIC. 
->Food items must be maintained with temperatures below 41F. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
Unlidded spray bottle of bleach and water mixture found stored on preparation table. Bottle noted without lid and being stored on table where active food preparation was observed. Staff indicated bleach is used for the bathrooms and other general cleaning. Please obtain bleach test strips if bleach is to be used as sanitizer. 
->Toxic materials must be used so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles.  Reference 7-202.12.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
Observed no QUAT test kit for the facility. Provide a QUAT test kit.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed no paper towels at the handwashing sink in the back. The paper towels were replaced during the inspection.
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed caulk coming apart from the wall near the prep line. Recaulk the handwashing sink to the wall.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.comment:
Observed coats stored on racks where there is food. Personal items and food must be stored separate than food.
750-1280 Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.
